LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Seattle has struggled a bit on offense, as Sam Darnold has not looked as sharp as he did last season. Darnold had a glute injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for a game, but he has started three games in a row for Seattle, leading it to a 1-2 record. Seattle still remains an elite defensive team, ranking No. 1 in the league in yards per play allowed and EPA/Play this season. The Denver defense (11th in EPA/Play and success rate) is off to a strong start as well, but the offense has lagged behind. Bo Nix is really struggling in his third NFL season, and Denver is averaging the seventh-fewest yards per play (4.7) in the NFL. Denver and Seattle both have playoff expectations – and Super Bowl hopes – in the 2026 season, but their offenses have to improve to make those dreams a reality. With Denver banged up a bit in the secondary on Thursday, Seattle has a shot to get back on track. It won’t be easy, though, as the Broncos are 2-0 at home with impressive victories against Jacksonville and the Los Angeles Rams. away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Starting cornerback Riley Moss, who missed last weekend's game with a rib injury, is questionable after being listed as limited in practice all week. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee, limited participation) CB Riley Moss (ribs, limited participation) Tuesday's injury report, which like Monday's is an estimation of participation, was mostly unchanged from a day earlier. Guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) went from being listed as limited Monday to full participation Tuesday, while every other player's status stayed the same. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, was listed as limited for the second straight day due to an ankle injury, as was defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Receiver Irv Charles, who was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day, was again listed as a full participant, another indicator that he is on track to make his Seahawks debut on Thursday. For the Broncos, two starters in the secondary, cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were listed as non-participants for the second straight day. The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions. away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

away.headline: Chicago Bears defeat Atlanta Falcons 31-23 as quarterback Caleb Williams returns from injury
away.blurb: Bears fans celebrate Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday night matchup Share ATLANTA -- Caleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, D'Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns and the Chicago Bears beat the Atlanta Falcons 31-23 on Sunday. Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon, who was activated from the physically unable to perform list before the game in his return from a calf injury, had three sacks and two forced fumbles. Gordon's big day was capped by a sack of Michael Penix Jr. and forced fumble with 2:54 remaining and the Bears protecting a 31-23 lead. The fumble was recovered by Devin Bush at the Atlanta 28. The Bears ran out the clock inside the Atlanta 5. After missing three games, Williams was both mobile and accurate in his impressive return for the Bears (4-2). He opened the game by completing 6 of 6 passes for 64 yards, including a 14-yard scoring pass to Colston Loveland, on Chicago's opening drive. Williams was 12 of 12 for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion in the second quarter. Though the Bears won two of three games with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum filing in at quarterback, Williams' return sparked the offense. He completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards with one touchdown. Penix threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Jahan Dotson in the second quarter. The perfectly placed back-shoulder fade pass cut the Bears' lead to 14-7, but a fumbled fair catch attempt by Zachariah Branch gave Chicago possession at the Atlanta 10 late in the first half. Branch also lost a fumble on a kickoff return late in the third quarter. Bears fans celebrate win, Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday "Caleb balled out," Hasler said. away.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon ties NFL record with monster game in return from injury vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Related: Bears’ Caleb Williams reached out to ‘John Wick’ for motivation before Falcons clash Chicago Bears fifth-year cornerback Kyler Gordon made an immediate impact in his first appearance of the 2026 season , recording three sacks and forcing two fumbles during Sunday afternoon’s 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons . The 26-year-old missed the first five games because of a calf injury before returning to help Chicago improve to 4-2. Gordon’s three sacks tied the NFL record for the most by a defensive back in a single game since sacks became an official statistic in 1982, according to NFL Researcher. The accomplishment was all the more extraordinary considering he had accumulated just 2.5 sacks across his previous 45 regular-season appearances. Gordon repeatedly disrupted Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. His first sack came early in the third quarter on a second-and-9 situation, helping the Bears force a turnover on downs shortly afterward. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He continued applying pressure on the Falcons’ following possession, bringing down Penix and forcing a fumble on third down. Although the Atlanta recovered the loose ball, the Falcons were forced to punt on the next play. Gordon’s most important contribution came with 2:54 remaining in the fourth quarter. With Chicago’s lead reduced to 31-23, Gordon notched another strip-sack, and linebacker Devin Bush recovered the fumble at Atlanta’s 28-yard line. The Bears subsequently ran down the clock inside the Falcons’ 5-yard line to clinch the victory. Gordon also logged two quarterback hits and tackled running back Bijan Robinson for a loss on a third-down play in the second quarter. The performance marked Gordon’s first game since dealing with multiple soft-tissue injuries last season. He signed a three-year, $40 million contract extension with Chicago before the 2025 season and had spent two separate periods on injured reserve. Quarterback Caleb Williams also returned from a hamstring injury after missing three games. He completed his first 12 passes for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion, finishing 30 of 36 for 305 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. His completion rate was 83.3%, and he had a 111.2 passer rating. Running back D’Andre Swift scored twice, while Roschon Johnson added another rushing touchdown. The two backs combined for 99 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Chicago took a 31-7 lead before Atlanta scored twice in the fourth quarter, with Penix finishing 19 of 33 for 225 yards and three touchdowns. Despite surrendering the late scores, the Bears held on for their fourth win. Chicago will next host the New England Patriots on Thursday night in the first of three consecutive prime-time contests. home.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

home.headline: Chicago Bears defeat Atlanta Falcons 31-23 as quarterback Caleb Williams returns from injury
home.blurb: Bears fans celebrate Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday night matchup Share ATLANTA -- Caleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, D'Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns and the Chicago Bears beat the Atlanta Falcons 31-23 on Sunday. Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon, who was activated from the physically unable to perform list before the game in his return from a calf injury, had three sacks and two forced fumbles. Gordon's big day was capped by a sack of Michael Penix Jr. and forced fumble with 2:54 remaining and the Bears protecting a 31-23 lead. The fumble was recovered by Devin Bush at the Atlanta 28. The Bears ran out the clock inside the Atlanta 5. After missing three games, Williams was both mobile and accurate in his impressive return for the Bears (4-2). He opened the game by completing 6 of 6 passes for 64 yards, including a 14-yard scoring pass to Colston Loveland, on Chicago's opening drive. Williams was 12 of 12 for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion in the second quarter. Though the Bears won two of three games with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum filing in at quarterback, Williams' return sparked the offense. He completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards with one touchdown. Penix threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Jahan Dotson in the second quarter. The perfectly placed back-shoulder fade pass cut the Bears' lead to 14-7, but a fumbled fair catch attempt by Zachariah Branch gave Chicago possession at the Atlanta 10 late in the first half. Branch also lost a fumble on a kickoff return late in the third quarter. Bears fans celebrate win, Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday "Caleb balled out," Hasler said. "Bears played great and yeah bears are back in town ready for Thursday." Fans are already looking ahead to Thursday's game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field, anticipating another lively atmosphere as the Bears return home. Bears: DB Cam Lewis was evaluated for a concussion in the second quarter. RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) was inactive. RG Jonah Jackson was ruled doubtful to return with a hip injury in the third quarter. Falcons: ILB Kendal Daniels was carted off the field midway through the third quarter after making a helmet-first tackle on tight end Colston Loveland. Daniels' head snapped back and Falcons players circled Daniels as he was strapped onto the stretcher and driven off the field. He was officially ruled out with a neck injury and the Falcons announced he was alert and had movement in all extremities and was being evaluated at Grady Hospital in Atlanta . ... ILB Divine Deablo (arm) was ruled out in the second quarter. CB Avieon Terrell (left shoulder) left the game in the second quarter. DB Billy Bowman Jr. was ruled doubtful with a hamstring injury. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Obviously, the buck stops with the head coach, but why did offensive coordinator David Blough call a play that USED MOTION as precious seconds ticked off the clock, and how was quarterbac

Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source. pic.twitter.com/O82hES7z4t After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved to 4.5 and now all the way to 5.5 following Adam Schefter's report. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites, a full one-point change from where the spread was on Tuesday morning . Still, Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday, which makes his status for Sunday a little murky. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that the two-time league MVP is "day-to-day." Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. While it would have been a positive sign for the Ravens for Jackson to practice on Wednesday, he still has time to log a session on Thursday or Friday before the team's matchup against Cleveland. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out
away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about the defender, saying he is excited to get him back out on the field. Joining Jackson is rookie tight end Matt Hibner, who suffered a hand injury. Reports indicate that Hibner has a cast on his hand, pointing to what could be a significant injury. There are no other red flags unless Jones or Vorhees are both unable to play, which would put the Baltimore offensive line in a very tough spot.

away.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for the Colts’ Week 6 Battle with the Titans Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Indianapolis Colts are heading into Week 6 looking to put last Sunday's loss to Pittsburgh behind them and get back in the win column. A matchup with the Tennessee Titans presents an opportunity to do just that, with Indianapolis entering as the clear favorite against its division rival. But divisional games rarely follow a predictable script, and the Colts have plenty to prove as they look to build on their iffy start to the season. With another week of football ahead, here are four bold predictions for Sunday's matchup in Nashville. Red Zone Struggles Will Continue Through the first five games, the Colts red zone offense has been ultra-reliable. Indianapolis ranks eighth in the NFL in red zone scoring percentage, finding the end zone 66.7% of the time. But that efficiency took a hit in Pittsburgh.The Colts drove into the red zone on three separate occasions, but only found the end zone once. I expect those struggles to continue, despite facing a Tennessee defense that’s allowing red zone touchdowns at a 62.5% clip. The Steelers exposed the blueprint the Colts have been using by loading the defensive front with physical run stuffers and keeping gains to a minimum against the run. Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) throws in the second quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. John Lanfranca Sun, October 18, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans (0-5) and Indianapolis Colts (2-3) will clash in Week 6 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Colts are 6.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the over/under set at 43.5 total points. Indianapolis is a -280 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is priced as a +230 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Colts predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Titans vs Colts pick: Titans +7 (-120) My Colts vs. Titans best bet is Tennessee to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Titans vs Colts Odds for NFL Week 6 Titans vs Colts spread: Titans +6.5 (-105), Colts -6.5 (-115) Titans vs Colts total: over/under 43.5 Titans vs Colts moneyline: Titans +230, Colts -280 Tennessee Titans vs Indianapolis Colts Preview The Titans may be near the bottom of any NFL power rankings you come across, but there is plenty of reason to believe they can compete with the Colts — and potentially pull the outright upset today. Indianapolis shouldn't be a touchdown favorite against any NFL team, even in a game it is projected to win on home turf. Let's start with what the Colts do well: run the football. Tennessee is sixth in the league defending the run on a per-carry basis despite playing from behind consistently. Even in a blowout loss to the Texans a week ago, the Titans limited the run effectively. It is evident they are playing the run more soundly this season — the Texans averaged just 2.9 yards per carry on 27 rushing attempts . In Week 4, Derrick Henry carried the ball 23 times against the Titans but averaged just 3.2 yards per rush. The Colts' Jonathan Taylor is an excellent back, but even he will struggle to gain consistent yardage if he is hit at or behind the line of scrimmage, something that has happened on 50% of his carries this season. The offensive line play for the Colts has been subpar through five games. Center Tanor Bortolini has played considerably worse this season than last, grading out 28th out of 34 qualifying players at the position, per Pro Football Focus. His matchup with Jeffery Simmons is one he simply cannot win on his own. Bortolini will need constant help with double teams in his attempt to negate the havoc Simmons can create. The issue for the Colts' front is that Simmons has John Franklin-Myers as his interior running mate. Both Franklin-Myers and Simmons rank inside the top 10 at the position this season in rush defense grade, per PFF. Running the ball is crucial for the Colts because their air attack lacks an explosive element without Alec Pierce in the lineup. In total, Indy ranks 30th in expected points added (EPA) as a passing offense. Daniel Jones has yet to crack seven yards per attempt in any game this season. Jones has a 4.6% turnover-worthy throw rate in comparison to a minuscule 2.0% big-time throw rate. Also, 19.9% of Jones' passes have been deemed off-target. That puts him in a tier with other quarterbacks who lead the league in inaccurate passes, with the only discernible difference being that the handful of other signal callers joining him in that tier have a considerably higher average depth of target . Cam Ward's performance to begin his second season with the Titans hasn't been very encouraging. However, this is by far the easiest matchup he has had this year. Ward's passer rating from a clean pocket sits at a respectable 96.1. It is pressure that gives him fits. The good news for the Tennessee offense here is that no team struggles to generate pressure more than Indianapolis. The Colts' pressure rate of 23% ranks last in the NFL. In fact, the gap between their pressure rate and the Cardinals ' pressure rate — the team that ranks 31st — is the same margin between the team ranking 14th ( Commanders ) and Arizona. Ward will have time to operate inside the pocket and the likelihood of him committing a game-changing turnover diminishes greatly in an environment in which he should be protected. In addition to lacking a pass rush, the Colts also rank last in the league in EPA/play when defending the run this season. Opposing rushers are averaging 2.4 yards before contact per rush against (31st). Titans vs Colts Pick, Betting Analysis You don't get many opportunities like this when diving into the ultra-tight market that is the NFL. We are able to back a team with a full touchdown worth of points in a divisional game where they are playing an opponent near the bottom of the league in passing offense, rushing defense, and pass rush production. There are a few books offering the Titans at +7 with added juice of just a few cents. I'd be willing to take the +7 at -120 or better; otherwise, +6.5 at -110 will suffice in getting us to the betting window to cash our ticket. The New England Patriots return home as -7.5 favorites, and they're looking to secure their third consecutive victory while hosting the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on Sunday afternoon. With both AFC East rivals showcasing stout defensive units capable of locking down opposing playmakers, my top Jets vs. Patriots predictions are locking in on a low-scoring affair. Here are my best bets and NFL picks for today. TOP Pick Jets vs Patriots prediction today: Under 43.5 The New York Jets may be better than their 2-3 record suggests, but only because of their defense. The Jets offense averages 5.1 yards per play, 22nd in the NFL, and ranks 28th in scoring at 18.6 ppg. The New England Patriots have turned the ball over on offense over the last two weeks, but they aren't as good as the 37.0 ppg they've averaged in that span, and they aren't as bad as the 12.0 ppg they put up before that. The New York defense is top three in the NFL in yards allowed per play (4.9) and yards allowed per passing attempt (5.5), which should tamp down on Drake Maye's outstanding numbers over the past two weeks. I'm backing the Under to 42.5 points. Jets vs Patriots combo I'm not expecting many points in this game, and on its face, that makes me suspicious of a spread of more than a touchdown. Even in the Jets' three losses this year, they've only lost by more than one score once in a 23-12 defeat to the Chicago Bears . I'm taking New York to cover. One area where the Patriots might consistently succeed is the running game, where the Jets allow 4.2 yards per rush. Rhamondre Stevenson is coming off a 64-yard performance against the Las Vegas Raiders last week, and I see him hitting the 60+ yard target on the ground again on Sunday. Rhamondre Stevenson Over 62.5 rushing yards Jets vs Patriots touchdown scorer: Hunter Henry Hunter Henry has had his two most productive games of the year over the past two weeks. He caught 8 passes for 106 yards and scored a touchdown last Sunday against the Raiders. The Jets haven't allowed a tight end touchdown yet this year, but have given up 22 catches for 183 yards to the group . New England won't spring many explosive plays against New York's secondary, and Henry will get plenty of red-zone targets. I like Henry to score a touchdown at 36% or lower. New York ranks eighth in the NFL in third-down defensive efficiency and sixth in red-zone defense, meaning it consistently forces opponents to settle for field goals — and you usually need to cash in a high of touchdown opportunities to cover a spread this large. Offensively, the Jets are still dealing with key injuries — Breece Hall , Adonai Mitchell, and Kenyon Sadiq are likely out — but they are getting Mason Taylor back. Hall's backup, Braelon Allen, also impressed against the Browns last week, rushing for 116 yards and a touchdown. Despite the missing pieces, New York's defense should be good enough to keep this game within a touchdown. Patriots Preview The Patriots are coming off a massive pair of wins after upsetting the Bills 29-26, and then dominating the Raiders 45-17 — but this is a classic spot to fade them. Historically, fading teams coming off huge scoring outputs hits at a 45% lifetime rate. Drake Maye is coming off a 99th-percentile performance, which is nearly impossible for any QB to replicate. The resurgent Maye was 26-for-34 passing against the Raiders, racking up 374 yards and four touchdowns with no turnovers. He added 25 rushing yards and a touchdown. New England's underlying metrics, however, are concerning: the offense ranks 20th on third down and 18th in the red zone. With TreVeyon Henderson ruled out, the Patriots' rushing attack plummets to 27th in success rate and 23rd in EPA and heavily reliant on Rhamondre Stevenson. Jets vs Patriots Spread Pick to Make I am taking the Jets to cover. We are getting the hook on a critical key number against a New England team primed for regression. The Patriots will likely have a tough time sustaining drives on the ground without TreVeyon Henderson, and Drake Maye could struggle against a Jets defense that excels on third downs. Expect New York to win some key moments throughout this game and cover the spread in this rivalry game. Pick: Jets +7.5 (-120) Editor's Note: This pick was made before reports of the Patriots likely activating WR A.J. Brown. My guess is Cooper mixes in both outside and in the slot — this is one of those situations with a really wide range of outcomes. It absolutely wouldn't shock me if the Jets ease Cooper back in and he plays limited snaps. But I also feel like I'm already being fairly conservative projecting a first-round pick who should eventually dominate snaps over Patrick/Williams-type players when fully healthy. The game environment could help. I have the Jets trailing at a much higher rate than usual here, which should naturally create more 3-WR sets, and if Christian Gonzalez is spending most of his time on Garrett Wilson, that could help Cooper find softer matchups elsewhere. I have Cooper's median closer to 22 receiving yards, so I'm showing a ton of value on 13.5 — but the range of outcomes is obviously massive. away.headline: New York Jets May Face A.J. Brown in New England Patriots Game - Report
away.blurb: Brown was listed as questionable on the Patriots injury report, and the team has not yet officially confirmed his return. If he does play, he opens up a major downfield threat for the Patriots. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got off to a bad start this season, with just one touchdown pass in the first three games to go with six interceptions. But he rallied to form in back-to-back wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders, racking up 643 passing yards to go with seven touchdowns against just one interception. away.blurb: Miami's most immediate concern is the group that missed or was limited during Tuesday's voluntary bye-week work. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks was absent after dealing with a foot issue during the Cincinnati game. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea also did not practice after leaving Sunday with an ankle injury. Coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Savaiinaea was doing OK, but his availability will not become clearer until Miami resumes normal game-week work. Running back Jaylen Wright, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out Tuesday. Wright played against Cincinnati after being listed with a foot injury. Beal has been dealing with a hamstring injury, Taylor with a quadriceps problem and Douglas with an ankle injury. The secondary has additional questions. JuJu Brents left the Bengals game with a stinger after earning the game's highest Pro Football Focus grade. Safety Michael Taaffe was listed with a chest injury. Cornerback Storm Duck and Darrell Baker Jr. are eligible to return from reserve lists, but eligibility does not guarantee immediate activation. Tight end Justin Joly remains in the concussion protocol. Running back De'Von Achane is on injured reserve with a knee injury and is not expected to return for the Jets game. Miami also continues to carry Ronnie Harrison Jr., Kyle Louis, Trey Moore, Rene Konga and Cole Turner on reserve lists. The matchup consequence is clearest in the trenches and secondary. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to handle a primary receiver, this time Garrett Wilson. The next reliable checkpoint comes when Miami returns to practice. Until then, no player should be described as officially out or cleared for Week 7 unless the club announces it. The Saints have the league’s 20th-ranked offense (322.0 yards per game) and the 25th-ranked defense (361.0 yards per game) as they head into MetLife Stadium against a Giants team that has a chance to go 4-0 at home for the first time since 2008, when they got off to a 6-0 start at home. Despite the Saints’ struggles, they enter this game as a 1.5-point favorite per FanDuel , which is a head-scratcher considering they have averaged 21.3 points in their last three games, while the home team has averaged 25 points per game. But odds aside, the NFC East-leading Giants’ goal, according to head coach John Harbaugh, is simple: stack wins. “You always know what they are, but you know you’ve got to stack wins to make the December standings matter,” Harbaugh said when asked how much he pays attention to the standings at this point in the season. “So, we focus on the next game.” The Giants, according to Tankathon , have to make hay, so to speak. They face a remaining schedule with a combined winning percentage of .484, with their four toughest opponents being the 49ers, Jaguars, Lions, and Browns. All four of those challenging opponents land on the schedule after the Giants’ Week 8 bye. But to focus on what the Giants might do this week, let’s look at the best- and worst-case scenarios. If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. It also ranks last in the league in defensive rush success (52.5%), meaning it struggles to stop opponents from gaining the minimum required yardage on a run (excluding kneeldowns and scrambles). The Giants’ rushing offense has not been the same since quarterback Jaxson Dart landed on IR with a season-ending knee injury. Although it ranks 17th in total rushing yards, it also averages a dismal 3.7 yards per attempt, 24th in the league. As if the rushing game’s struggles aren’t enough, it will be interesting to see if Harbaugh decides to reduce running back Cam Skattebo’s touches this week given his fumbling issue. As usual, the head coach was mum on the plans, but this could be a week when Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. get bigger roles in the rushing attack to see if they can jumpstart it. On the defensive side, the Giants’ pass rush has finally awakened after a slow start, recording seven sacks over the last two weeks. This week, they face a Saints offensive line that has surrendered three sacks to quarterback Tyler Shough over that same period. Combine that with the opportunistic Giants secondary, which has forced eight turnovers this season , against a Saints offense that has committed 13 giveaways, and the Giants’ quest to remain undefeated at home could get a lot easier. The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. There are many reasons for the Giants’ struggles in run defense, but one glaring issue has been facing pre-snap motion. Motion changes the look for the defense and has sometimes left players out of position or forced them into bad angles as they try to stop the play from gaining a lot of yards. Under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints have deployed pre-snap motion on 64% of their offensive snaps this season, the ninth-highest rate in the league, and have a 46% success rate overall when using motion. While they use pre-snap motion more in the passing game, they have used it at a 35% rate in the rushing game. If the Giants, who have allowed opponents 5.2 yards per rush attempt on first down, can’t tighten that up, the Saints will have options on subsequent downs, giving New Orleans an advantage. The other thing that could spoil the Giants’ quest to win their fourth straight game at home is their own aggressiveness on defense. If the Giants, who over the last two weeks have blitzed on 57.8% of opposing quarterbacks’ drop backs, come at the Saints with a similar rate of pressure, they’d better hope that Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough, who per PFF data, has a 102.7 passer rating when throwing the ball in 2.5 seconds or less, doesn’t connect with receivers Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed for the big pass plays downfield. If I live to be 100 (fingers crossed), I will never understand how the oddsmakers come up with their weekly point spreads. What I do understand is that Harbaugh has this team dialed in, and this matchup against the Saints is overall favorable for the Giants if they play a relatively clean game and keep the ball-security issues out of the mix. The Giants have a lot more going for them at this point in the season than the Saints, including far too many advantages that, if they hit on all cylinders, will get the job done. Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore. The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences. With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East. Here are our predictions for Sunday's game. Grant Chachere, Staff Writer: L 24-17 This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis . I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth. While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints. At the half, join us for Halftime Studs & Duds . Then, a fter the game, join us for our Biggest Winners & Biggest Losers , our View of the Game , and the Most Important Quotes from Kellen Moore & Players . Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble. I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out. Prediction: Giants 24, Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 21-17 Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three? We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust. Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are. Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. However, don't bet the house on who I choose to win today. I've only been right once in five prognostications this year. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Saints are 1.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 45.5 total points. New Orleans is a -115 moneyline favorite to win outright, while New York is listed as a -105 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Saints vs Giants predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Saints vs Giants Odds for NFL Week 6 Saints vs Giants spread: Saints -1.5, Giants +1.5 Saints vs Giants total: over/under 45.5 Saints vs Giants moneyline: Saints -115, Giants -105 New Orleans Saints vs New York Giants Preview The Saints originally opened as underdogs for this game, but almost immediately swung to 1.5-point road favorites — and I think they are sitting at the absolute bottom of their market value. Am I thrilled to back New Orleans on the road here? Not exactly. But I am itching to fade the Giants . Sure, the Saints' run defense is abysmal, but they are facing a Giants team entirely incapable of exploiting it. New Orleans has played a grueling schedule the last two weeks, facing the Falcons (who ran wild with Bijan Robinson) and the Vikings (who have one of the best defenses in the NFL). Offensively, Tyler Shough has been very good when kept clean in the pocket. With the Giants missing Brian Burns , Shough should have all day to operate and consistently move the ball through the air in this game. The Giants are a couple games above .500, but they are arguably the most fraudulent team in the NFL. They could easily be 1-4 right now after lucking out with a tie against the Commanders last week. New York's back-to-back home wins came against the Titans and Cardinals — two incompetent teams that turned the ball over at the goal line with a chance to win. Offensively, the Giants have completely stalled since losing Jaxson Dart. They rank 29th in both rush success rate and rush EPA, meaning their ground game has almost totally vanished. Jameis Winston has thrown for 694 yards with a 6:3 TD:INT ratio in the three games he's started. He's done a good job of feeding Malik Nabers as the Giants' WR1 has surpassed 100 receiving yards in each of the last two weeks. Of course, the thing with Winston is that he's prone to making critical mistakes when throwing into zone coverage. Saints vs Giants Pick, Betting Analysis There is a massive strength-of-schedule disparity here, with the Giants feasting on the easiest schedule in the league so far while the Saints have been heavily battle tested against some of the NFL's best. Without Jaxson Dart's mobility, the Giants simply haven't bee able to run the ball with Cam Skattebo, forcing Jameis Winston into high-variance, mistake-prone dropbacks. The Saints should be able to keep the pocket clean for Tyler Shough throughout this game, which will likely allow him to dissect the Giants' defense and lift his team to a road win. home.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
home.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster.
