LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. away.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
away.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are well outside the playoff picture in the NFC through six weeks, as they're just 1-5 after an overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Tampa Bay opened as a three-point underdog on the road in Week 7, and it has since moved to a 3.5-point underdog in the latest odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . At 1-5, the Bucs are +570 to make the playoffs and +12500 to win the Super Bowl, making them one of the bigger long shots in the NFL through six weeks. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. away.headline: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return
away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. Giants in a close one. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers. As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Steelers 24, Bucs 20 The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers. I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays. I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win. Overall Record: 3-2 James Hill, Writer: Steelers 21, Bucs 17 I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend. Overall record: 2-3 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 21, Steelers 14 So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week. Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon. Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win. Logan Robinson, Founder: Steelers 31, Bucs 24 This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh. I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season. I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter. River Wells, Editor: Steelers 24, Bucs 17 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better. The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters. On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too. The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it. Consensus: Steelers 4, Bucs 1 The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year? He graduated with a journalism degree from the University of Florida in 2021. You can follow him on Twitter @riverhwells. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. home.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
home.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. The Cardinals are massive underdogs entering Week 6, and perhaps rightfully so. Arizona's shown little to inspire upset hopes of a Rams team that's coming off a short week and a loss on Monday Night Football. National picks are heavily slanted towards Los Angeles: Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Rams Eva Geitheim: Rams Mitch Goldich: Rams Mike Kadlick: Rams Gilberto Manzano: Rams Conor Orr: Rams John Pluym: Rams Matt Verderame: Rams Maldonado's pick: Rams 28, Cardinals 7 Moody's pick: Rams 38, Cardinals 17 Walder's pick: Rams 31, Cardinals 16 FPI prediction: LAR, 87.3% (by an average of 11.9 points) It was a clean sweep of Rams picks again from Jeremy Bergman, Brooke Cersosimo, Gennaro Filice, Bobby Kownack, Dan Parr. Cersosimo provided an explanation as to why she chose Los Angeles: "Weird things happen in this league, but this one feels pretty straightforward. The Rams' offense is averaging 424.4 yards per game, and to be honest, it feels like they haven't come close to reaching peak performance in 2026. Sean McVay has a pick-your-poison attack that makes defenses pay on the regular, and Arizona's league-worst scoring defense will be no match for Matthew Stafford and Co. "On the other side of the ball, Los Angeles' defense has been steady, ranking third in yards allowed and fifth on third down, and should do enough to stall an Arizona offense that'll likely have its share of chunk plays featuring Trey McBride but ultimately won't sustain most drives. The Rams' biggest issue has been their special teams, and they didn't waste time replacing kicker Harrison Mevis for Blake Grupeafter Monday night's fiasco. We'll see if one change does the trick." Zach Berman: Rams Jon Greenberg: Rams Chad Graff: Rams Larry Holder: Rams Josh Kendall: Rams Steven Louis Goldstein: Rams Austin Mock: Rams Nick Kosmider: Rams Bleacher Report Gary Davenport: Cardinals Brad Gagnon: Rams Ian Hanford: Rams Kris Knox: Rams Moe Moton: Rams Wes O'Donnell: Rams Brent Sobleski: Rams Our Prediction Divisional battles are always tough, so there's credence to this being a close game. L.A. remains near the top of the odds in the Super Bowl market, but a few injuries – and some close losses – have dropped the Rams to 2-3 and in third place in the NFC West. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to Buffalo at home, yet it’s favored by double digits in this divisional battle with Jacoby Brissett and Co. The Cardinals shocked the NFL world in Week 1, upsetting the Los Angeles Chargers, but the Chargers’ 0-5 start has taken a little away from that victory. Since then, Arizona has lost four straight games, allowing over 30 points in all of them. Plus, the team traded away former top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Houston Texans. At some point, it feels like rookie Carson Beck will get a chance under center, as the Cards are destined for a top-five pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. So, do the Rams take care of business and cover at home? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game. It’s an exciting exercise that we hope will help guide bettors on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! As the Rams look to get back over .500, they are in desperate need of a get-right game against a weak division opponent. Here’s my final score prediction for this NFC West clash in Week 6. Cardinals vs. Rams Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cardinals +12.5 (-105) Rams -12.5 (-115) Cardinals: +600 51.5 (Over -115/Under -105) Even with the Rams’ loss to Buffalo on Monday night, the spread in this game has held steady at 12.5 with the Cardinals dropping four games in a row. The total has moved a point, going from 52.5 to 51.5 since Sunday night. Cardinals vs. Rams Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s betting on Arizona to cover the spread: The Rams have a glaring issue that cost them on Monday Night Football, and it's something that leads me to be cautious about betting on them to cover big spreads: their special teams. It's the worst special teams in the league and has been for the past couple of years. If they make another blunder in Week 6, it's going to tee the Cardinals up to at least cover this big point spread. The Cardinals' defense is one of the worst in the NFL, but they have enough weapons on offense that they should be able to be at least somewhat effective in this game against a Rams team on a short week. I'll take the points with Arizona. I see where MacMillan is coming from with this bet, but the Cardinals have been blown out by Seattle and Detroit this season, and their offense may struggle against a Rams defense that remains a top-five unit against the pass (fourth in EPA/Pass) in 2026. L.A.’s special teams issues are certainly worth looking at, but the Cardinals have allowed over 30 points to Detroit, the New York Giants, Seattle and San Francisco since their win over the Los Angeles Chargers. I expect this high-powered Rams attack to push 40 points in Week 6, and I’m not buying this Jacoby Brissett-led offense to put up enough points to cover on the road. Sean McVay gets his favorite NFC West opponent at an ideal time, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting a struggling Arizona Cardinals team at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18. Los Angeles is favored by 12.5 points this afternoon, and my Cardinals vs. Rams prediction and NFL picks expect the Rams to capitalize on an Arizona defense that has struggled to keep opponents off the scoreboard all season. TOP Pick Cardinals vs Rams prediction: Rams -12.5 As long as the Los Angeles Rams don't climb above -13.5, I'm laying it. Motivation is always a concern with a double-digit favorite, but Los Angeles is 2-3 and can't afford to let the San Francisco 49ers run away with the division. Despite the losing record, the Rams still rank second in my power ratings . Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals have lost four straight and failed to cover three of those contests , allowing an NFL-worst 32.4 points per game. The matchup gets worse without Arizona running back Jeremiyah Love . Los Angeles ranks third in quarterback pressure rate, according to Pro.NFL.com , which will make life miserable for quarterback Jacoby Brissett . Cardinals vs Rams combo Los Angeles can do most of the heavy lifting for this combo. If the Rams jump on Arizona early, Brissett will have to chase points while Matthew Stafford and the offense keep creating scoring opportunities. Los Angeles is 4-0 to the Over in its last four games against teams with a losing record. Eventually, Rams RB Kyren Williams will be in position to finish drives and help Los Angeles protect a comfortable lead on the ground. Williams has five total touchdowns in five games this season (four rushing and one receiving). Arizona doesn't need to turn this into a shootout, either. A couple of Cardinals touchdowns should be enough, as I'm expecting the Rams to put up points in the mid-30s. Kyren Williams anytime touchdown Cardinals vs Rams touchdown scorer: Michael Wilson I like Michael Wilson's anytime touchdown probability up to 33%, as I'm anticipating plenty of garbage time, while LA's offensive stars are too expensive for me as standalone touchdown picks. Wilson also has history in this matchup. He caught three touchdown passes in two games against the Rams last season and is already Arizona's most-targeted wide receiver. His opportunity should only grow after Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to Houston. If Arizona spends most of the second half chasing points, Wilson should see enough volume to give him a shot at finding the end zone. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love sits Wednesday
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn't lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. home.headline: Rams have a legitimate gripe with NFL officials, but their 2-4 record is the bigger problem
home.blurb: Rams kicker Blake Grupe knocks himself out of his debut with a disastrous tackle attempt Yes, a questionable personal foul helped Arizona get into position for the winning field goal in its 18-16 victory. Rams fans have every right to be frustrated, especially given what happened against Denver earlier this season. Rams kicker Blake Grupe had injured his knee tackling Devin Duvernay just over five minutes into the game and did not return, leaving punter Ethan Evans to attempt the crucial kick. The questionable call certainly helped Arizona. But the Rams had already given Brissett a free play and allowed a 21-yard completion on a drive that began with 47 seconds remaining and the Cardinals out of timeouts. Another questionable call, another loss Look, saying a team should have played better doesn't excuse a questionable call that helps decide the game. The officials still have a job to do, regardless of what happened before the flag. They're too talented to write off after six games. They're also 2-4, and the preseason hype isn't going to help them climb out of that hole. Zaven Collins also did not practice with a hip issue and is questionable. The other players questionable are punter Blake Gillikin (back) and safety Kitan Crawford (ankle). The Cardinals could activate Crawford to the roster by tomorrow afternoon. After not practicing all week, the team ruled out running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and safeties Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) and Dewey Wingard (knee). Quarterback Carson Beck had a back injury that made him limited on Friday. He did not receive a game designation. Sean McVay said cornerback Trent McDuffie pulled his groin at practice on Thursday and is listed as questionable. Safety Kam Curl is also questionable with a ankle issue. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not take part in practice on Thursday as he allows his ankle to heal. It's also looking bleak for safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) to play after logging another DNP. It was another limited practice for wide receiver Devin Duvernay (ribs) and safety Kitan Crawford (ankle). While game designations will be announced on Friday, the Cardinals have until Saturday to activate Crawford to the main roster if they want him to play this weekend. The Rams practiced for the first time this week. Safety Kam Curl was limited with an ankle injury. The ankle issue continues to linger for Jeremiyah Love. While the Cardinals running back has played through the discomfort, he did not practice on Wednesday. Coach Mike LaFleur emphasized caution and rest. Safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) also did not practice ahead of the Week 6 game against the Rams. Williams would need to progress through concussion protocol to play. Kitan Crawford had his 21-day practice window opened and returned to practice after exiting Week 1 with an ankle injury. He was limited. Wide receiver/returner Devin Duvernay (ribs) was also limited. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers: NFL Week 6 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the third time in five games to begin the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs will square off against an opponent from their own division. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group. With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like. Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season. If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe. Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances. Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters. Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles. This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender. The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart. The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising. Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment. Kenneth Walker III has totally transformed a Kansas City offense that ranks in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play and success rate in 2026. Led by Offensive Player of the Year favorite Kenneth Walker, they're a dangerous offense to face, and any game they're involved in shouldn't have a total in the low 40s. Unfortunately, the Chargers' offense is bad, but I continue to believe that Mike McDaniel's system is going to eventually click, and they're going to have some strong offensive outputs sooner rather than later. Now that they face an average Chiefs defense facing an 0-6 record to start the season, now could be the time that their offense comes out firing. While I don’t mind the OVER play, I think this is going to be a lopsided game, especially since Los Angeles is banged up across the board on offense. Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris have all been hurt in 2026, and the Chargers have tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve. That’s led to a terrible offense, as L.A. ranks 32nd in the NFL in EPA/Play and 28th in success rate through five weeks. As MacMillan mentioned, this Chiefs offense has been one of the best in the league, and I expect Patrick Mahomes and Co. to take care of business out of a bye week against a Chargers team that has a very slim chance of turning this season around. away.headline: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh provides injury updates on key players ahead of Week 6
away.blurb: The 24-year-old wide receiver was active but didn’t play a snap in the Chargers loss. Before their Week 5 contest, Harbaugh listed McConkey as week-to-week. He didn't practice Wednesday through Friday but was still listed as questionable. Los Angeles was already short on pass-catchers with Quentin Johnston ruled out with a chest injury. As for Bud Dupree, Harbaugh listed him as day-to-day, while Tre' Harris and Donte Jackson are week-to-week. Dupree injured his neck in the third quarter against the Broncos. Harris and Jackson are dealing with a hamstring injury. Harris suffered his injury in the third quarter of Week 5, while Jackson missed the entire contest after being held out of practice all week. Week 5 has come and gone for the Chargers, and they have yet to collect a win in 2026. The Chargers suffered a tough home loss to the Broncos , 23-17. They head into Week 6 without a win, and it doesn’t get any easier as they face the Chiefs. Los Angeles is as short-handed as it can get. A day after their Week 5 loss, Jim Harbaugh provided injury updates on key players, including Ladd McConkey. Harbaugh said they were using McConkey as an emergency option, and he’s hopeful that he can practice this week. Harbaugh also provided an update on offensive guard Kayode Awosika, saying that he is healing and rehabbing. Awosika has missed the last three games with a lower leg injury. Awosika's next chance to play will be in Week 6 against the Chiefs. The Chargers will hope for a cleaner injury report as the week progresses and they prepare for Week 6. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid gives injury updates on Jaylon Moore, Travis Kelce after Week 6 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers
away.blurb: Several Kansas City Chiefs players battled through bumps and bruises in their Week 6 victory. Andy Reid addressed a handful of them after the game, including one starter who was ruled out. Kansas City avoided any significant injuries against the Chargers. However, several players dealt with minor injuries and played through them during the game. Here's what Reid had to say, plus one notable name he left out. “As far as the injuries go, Jaylon Moore has a concussion,” Reid said. “That's the one that probably stands out the most. (Travis) Kelce tweaked his ankle there. Continued to play, might be a little sore tomorrow, but he did a nice job tonight. And then the rest of that, everybody worked out. I mean, (Jalen) Royals went into the tent to be checked for a concussion, but he was good there. And then Kingsley (Suamataia) got kicked in the calf, but he should be OK.” According to Reid, the most notable injury was the head injury to starting right tackle Jaylon Moore. Moore suffered a concussion during the game and was ruled out . Reid confirmed the diagnosis after the game. Moore was replaced by Joshua Ezeudu, who did a solid job filling in on both pass protection and the run game. Chiefs TE Travis Kelce toughed out an ankle injury during Week 6 Reid's update on Chiefs TE Travis Kelce was about what you'd expect. Kelce exited early with an ankle injury and hobbled to the sideline, where the training staff assisted him. He had his ankle wrapped and returned to the game. He then exited a second time to return to the training table and have the ankle rewrapped. Jaylen Royals and Kingsley Suamatia both return after brief absences Wide receiver Jalen Royals took a head hit and had to be checked out. NFL spotters pulled him from the game, and he went to the blue medical tent for a concussion evaluation. The NFL's independent neurologist ultimately cleared Royals to return. Still, the team will monitor him for any symptoms that show up once the practice week resumes ahead of Week 7's game. Reid's postgame update left one name out: starting cornerback Nohl Williams. Early in the game, Williams was injured after making a tackle for loss. It looked like a shoulder injury, possibly to the clavicle. Based on the TV replay, it didn't look good initially. However, Williams missed very little time. He returned on the ensuing series and was instrumental throughout the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Chargers. Reid's failure to mention the brief absence suggests this is a minor injury and not something that will keep Williams out going forward. It didn't keep him out against Los Angeles, and he contributed big, finishing with four total tackles, two passes defended, and a tackle for loss. It's a good sign for Kansas City that Williams, Royals, Suamataia, and Kelce all finished the game. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad. Kansas City and Los Angeles kick off Sunday’s game at 3:25 p.m. CT. It can be watched live in Kansas City and the surrounding viewing area on KCTV5.

They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3. Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8. Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league. While Vegas got off to a solid start this season, I think their recent stretch is a bit too much for them to attack. I think the last two losses may be hard to shake off. I think the Bills will start to shake off their ball security problems and Allen just seems to be unstoppable, even when he is committing turnovers. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. Wide receiver DJ Moore (shoulder), wide receiver Joshua Palmer (shoulder), defensive lineman Ed Oliver (knee), cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) and defensive lineman T.J. away.headline: Bills’ final DJ Moore, Ed Oliver injury updates for Week 6 vs. Raiders
away.blurb: Hours before kickoff, the organization shared its entire list of active players for the matchup against the Raiders. Moore and Oliver were not on the list , determining they are both officially ruled out for Sunday. Moore is dealing with an AC joint sprain in his shoulder. He's been in and out all season due to the injury. The 29-year-old has appeared in four games in his first year with the Bills, recording 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown. Quarterback Josh Allen will rely on a receiving group consisting of Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer, and Khalil Shakir against the Raiders. The Bills will kick off at 4:25 p.m. EST on Sunday against the Raiders. It will be the second straight road game for the franchise. They'll return to Buffalo in Week 8 after having a bye in Week 7. away.headline: Raiders final Week 6 injury report analysis vs Bills: Vegas top DT OUT
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The final injury report of the week is out for the Raiders . Three players are listed as being OUT for the game -- DT Tonka Hemingway, WR Dont'e Thornton, and TE Carter Runyon. The latter two have yet to be activated from injured reserve. The good news here is the return of Jalen Nailor who missed last week with a concussion. "Well, Jalen's [Nailor] a playmaker," said head coach Klint Kubiak on Friday. "He's going to help us. He's going to help us win a lot of games this year, and I think obviously you don't want him to be out for a game, but it gives him a chance to freshen up, and he'll be an impactful player for us." The Bills had four players Questionable for the game -- WR DJ Moore (shoulder), DT Ed Oliver (knee), WR Josh Palmer (shoulder), and DT TJ Sanders (shoulder). Hemingway missed all week in the concussion protocol. He will miss the game, leaving the Raiders without their best interior defensive lineman. #Raiders #Bills Friday injury report. "Tonka's [Hemingway] been a very steady leader for us," said Kubiak. "He had a really good April, a really good training camp. We're going to miss Tonka this week, but it's opportunities for others." Those who will see increased "opportunities" include Adam Butler, Folorunso Fatukasi, Thomas Booker IV, and Jonah Laulu. The team could activate JJ Pegues as well. The fellow 2025 draft pick has been inactive for all but one game this season.

away.headline: Raiders Get Major Ashton Jeanty Injury Update Ahead of Bills Game
away.blurb: The news comes just one day after questions surfaced about whether Las Vegas would consider resting Jeanty to allow his injuries additional time to heal. However, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak quickly dismissed that possibility Wednesday, making it clear that the team expects its starting running back to be available against Buffalo. Jeanty was listed as questionable against New England after missing Friday's practice but was ultimately cleared to participate. However, his production was limited in the Raiders' 45-17 loss. home.headline: There's a new narrative regarding Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty, and it doesn't look good at the moment
home.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders continue to struggle to close out games. This time, they lost 33-30 to the Buffalo Bills . Sure, that's impressive considering where the Bills are as a franchise and where the Raiders are in their rebuild . But at some point they have to figure out how to win games. And it would help if the run game was better. Against the Kansas City Chiefs , they rushed for 72 yards on 26 attempts. Against the New England Patriots , they had just 38 on 18 attempts. Against the Bills, a known bad defense, they rushed for 60 yards on 20 attempts. That's just unacceptable. And some of it is coming back to Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders did find a way to get their rookie running back in the game, though. They even had him out there in the pass game. And that changes everything. Before, he was usually only out there on running plays, and it started to become a bit telegraphed. He had his biggest reception of the season on Sunday for seven yards. That doesn't seem like much, but it keeps the defense on its toes. When you have Jeanty out there, and you're running and passing to him, but Washington usually only comes in when it's time to run, the defense can easily start to guess what you're doing. "He gave us a spark; he did some good stuff for us," Kubiak told reporters when asked about running back Mike Washington Jr. He's a player with very high potential. And he can be a weapon for the Raiders. But he can't do any of that if they don't put him on the field. Then again, that means taking your No. 6 overall pick from last season, Jeanty, off the field. So, Vegas has to figure out how to balance that better while also riding the hot hand in the running game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Obviously, the buck stops with the head coach, but why did offensive coordinator David Blough call a play that USED MOTION as precious seconds ticked off the clock, and how was quarterbac

picks.headline: Who Experts Are Picking For Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers in Week 6
picks.blurb: Who Experts Are Picking For Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers in Week 6 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers enter their Week 6 contest at Lambeau Field on Sunday night coming off very different Week 5 showings. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. The Packers defeated the Bears, 31-7. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Pete Prisco: Packers Jared Dubin: Packers Ryan Wilson: Packers John Breech: Cowboys Tyler Sullivan: Cowboys Dave Richard: Packers Jamey Eisenberg: Packers Pete Prisco: Packers Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) celebrates during the game between the Cowboys and the Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jeremy Bergman: Packers Brooke Cersosimo: Packers Gennaro Filice: Packers Bobby Kownack: Cowboys Dan Parr: Packers Jeremy Bergman: Packers Final expert tally and my prediction Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Packers: 26 The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air . The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. Final score prediction: Packers 30, Cowboys 27 Published Oct 16, 2026 MIKE MORAITIS Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report. away.headline: Turpin Cowboys injury clouds return game after opening kickoff hit
away.blurb: Turpin Cowboys injury clouds return game after opening kickoff hit Share Advertisement The Dallas Cowboys lost one of their most dangerous return threats before they had run an offensive snap against the Green Bay Packers. KaVontae Turpin was hurt on the opening kickoff Sunday night and was listed as questionable to return. The injury landed immediately in the spot where Turpin does his most damage. He is the Cowboys' primary return specialist, and the loss matters fast because the game had barely started when he was being walked to the locker room. Turpin's absence would be a real hit because he has become one of the most productive return men in football. He led the NFL in kickoff return yards in 2024, earned All-Pro honors for the first time that season and is a two-time Pro Bowler heading into his fifth season with the Cowboys. The team also has a fresh reason to watch his status closely after his three-year, $13.5 million extension in March 2025 and his July 2025 arrest on drug and weapons charges in Texas. For now, the immediate question is not whether the Cowboys can replace him for one play. It is whether they can keep the game from turning without the weapon that set their return unit apart before the night was even underway. Is Dj Moore Playing This Week? Cowboys Injury Report Rules Out Starting Cornerback for Packers Game 2 Cowboys Miss Thursday Practice, DeMarvion Overshown Progressing In New Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Colts fire long-time GM Chris Ballard Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown during the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Josh Sanchez Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:16 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads A new week of NFL action officially kicks off on Thursday night in primetime, marking exactly one week since the last time we saw the Dallas Cowboys on the field . Last Thursday did not go as planned for Dallas, as the team suffered an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, but the team gets an opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 with another primetime showdown. This weekend, Dallas will make the trip to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Green Bay Packers . On Thursday afternoon, the Cowboys returned to the practice field and dropped their latest injury report . On Wednesday, five players did not participate in practice, but on Thursday, that number was down to two. Dallas Cowboys Week 6 Injury Report - Thursday The two players who did not participate in Thursday afternoon's practice are cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton, who are both dealing with hamstring injuries. Along with Overshown, Miller, and Speed improving their participation statuses on Thursday, there was another player who took a positive step forward: star cornerback Joey Porter Jr ., whose home debut was spoiled last week after a sudden illness. But after some extra time to recover from the issues that left him throwing up in the locker room before being sent home , he is feeling well and on track to play on Sunday night. Porter was listed on Wednesday's report with an ankle issue, but it is not serious, and he will be in line for an increased workload this week. Per reports, Porter is expected to have a "near full workload" in Week 6 . Hopefully, everyone will continue improving as the week continues, with just two days remaining until game day. Kick off between the Cowboys and Packers at Lambeau Field is set for 8:20 p.m. Et on NBC and Peacock. away.headline: Packers vs. Cowboys: Breaking down final injury report of Week 6
away.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. home.blurb: Hopefully, Green Bay can avoid any more serious injuries. On the positive side, they are expecting to get two key contributors back very soon. It has recently been reported that Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs will return as the starting running back in Week Seven. Additionally, All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons is getting closer and closer to his own return. However, the Packers have not opened up his practice window as they want to ensure that he is 100% healthy and not at risk for any soft tissue injuries because of rushing a return to the field. “A league source tells me Parsons might not return until Week 9, against the Patriots on Nov. 8. In Week 7, Green Bay plays the Detroit Lions before hosting the Panthers on “’Thursday Night Football’; believing Parsons needs more than a week to ramp up, the short-week turnaround would be difficult to pull off.” If this is truly the targeted return date, it would be realistic to see Parsons designated for return by Green Bay this week. This means he would be able to practice with the rest of the team, and the Packers would have 21 days to add him to the active roster. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. The Green Bay Packers have lost several players to season-ending injuries already this year. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. Parsons, who was acquired prior to the start of the 2025 season in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys, tore his ACL in late in the year and has missed every game of 2026 thus far.
