That said, Tennessee is going nowhere fast, while the Packers are losing defensive linemen at an alarming rate. Imagine a defensive line with Simmons and Micah Parsons both rushing the opposing QB. That would make DC Jonathan Gannon's play-calling job on defense quite easy. The NFL trade deadline is in mid-November, but as real NFC contenders like the Green Bay Packers start to emerge over the next few weeks, it's plausible to speculate that fireworks could take place across the trade landscape. Commanders vs 49ers prediction: Under 52.5 This total was 49.5 on the lookahead and has crept as high as 52.5 as of Saturday, which is too much for me. I'm backing the Under, with THE BLITZ projecting 49.4 points on Monday night. There are just too many health concerns surrounding key offensive players to get excited about an Over this high, especially given that this is the highest total either team has seen all year. Mike Evans was a DNP with multiple injuries on Friday, and Deebo Samuel is out. Add in the injuries to Demarcus Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, and Christian Kirk, and the 49ers might be rolling with WR8 and WR9 on their depth chart. Washington could also have trouble moving the ball, and I doubt San Francisco is going to let Jayden Daniels run for another 100+ yards. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has not practiced this week, while his backups, Austin Ekeler and Rachaad White, have both been limited . Stefon Diggs logged his first limited practice since Week 4, and Terry McLaurin is getting veteran rest after failing to handle his full workload in Week 5. Throw in double-digit winds and cross-country travel for the visitors, and there are too many red flags for me to back points on Monday night. I'd play this Under down to 50.5. Commanders vs 49ers combo I'm running the double quarterback touchdown combo every Monday night, and this might be the most optimistic I've been all season, as both Brock Purdy and Jayden Daniels are carrying legitimate scoring probabilities. away.headline: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL’s ‘Next Great’ Cornerback
away.blurb: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL's ‘Next Great' Cornerback The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants , in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. "SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week." By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. "Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day," The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return." Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 11:27pm Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions . Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Play Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders "Trey Amos has no hobbies," Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. "No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back." Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. "My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. Amos started training camp on the PUP list but returned to practice a few weeks later … and automatically got hurt again. away.headline: San Francisco 49ers Make Mike Evans Announcement Before Commanders Game
away.blurb: San Francisco designated Evans as questionable for its October 19 matchup against the Washington Commanders, the team confirmed Saturday. Evans has been dealing with rib and Achilles injuries that kept him out of practice Thursday and Friday. The designation means Evans has not been ruled out, although the 49ers are not guaranteeing that he will play. Evans was among six players listed as questionable on San Francisco's final injury report, joining wide receiver Christian Kirk (calf), defensive tackle Gracen Halton (quad), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder), defensive back Siran Neal (neck) and defensive lineman Mykel Williams (knee). His prediction has already proven accurate in two respects. The 49ers ruled Bosa out with knee and calf injuries, while Juszczyk is expected to return after missing Week 5 with a knee injury. San Francisco also ruled out Deebo Samuel because of a hamstring injury suffered against the Seattle Seahawks . His absence raises the stakes for Evans, who has emerged as one of Brock Purdy's most productive targets this season. Kirk's questionable designation presents another variable. He practiced on a limited basis throughout the week as San Francisco continues evaluating his potential return. Evans has not been ruled out, but his questionable designation means the 49ers have not committed to playing him against Washington. Until then, Evans remains questionable, with the 49ers hoping their most productive receiver can deliver another performance like the one that helped them beat Seattle.
